## 1️⃣ Yöntem – Tkinter (Standart Kütüphane)

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-

"""
Karanlık temalı, tuşlu ve gelişmiş bir hesap makinesi.
Tkinter (Python'un standart GUI kütüphanesi) ile hazırlanmıştır.
"""

import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import ttk
import math

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. HESAP MAKİNESİ SINİFİ
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
class DarkCalculator(tk.Tk):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()

        # --------------------------------------------------------------
        # Pencere ayarları
        # --------------------------------------------------------------
        self.title("Dark Theme Calculator")
        self.resizable(False, False)
        self.geometry("360x530")
        self.configure(bg="#2e2e2e")           # ana arka plan rengi (koyu)

        # --------------------------------------------------------------
        # Stil (ttk) → Karanlık tema renkleri
        # --------------------------------------------------------------
        style = ttk.Style(self)
        style.theme_use('clam')

        # Genel renkler
        self.bg_color      = "#2e2e2e"   # pencere arka planı
        self.display_bg    = "#1e1e1e"
        self.button_bg     = "#3b3b3b"
        self.button_fg     = "#e0e0e0"
        self.button_active = "#5a5a5a"
        self.special_bg    = "#ff9500"  # eşittir (=) ve temizle (C) butonları
        self.special_fg    = "#ffffff"

        # Stil ayarları (buton, etiket vb.)
        style.configure(
            "TButton",
            font=("Helvetica", 14),
            foreground=self.button_fg,
            background=self.button_bg,
            borderwidth=0,
            focusthickness=0,
            focuscolor=self.button_bg,
            padding=10,
        )
        style.map("TButton",
                  background=[("active", self.button_active)])

        style.configure(
            "Display.TLabel",
            font=("Helvetica", 24),
            foreground="#ffffff",
            background=self.display_bg,
            padding=12,
            anchor="e"
        )

        # --------------------------------------------------------------
        # DISPLAY (Ekran)
        # --------------------------------------------------------------
        self.expression = tk.StringVar()
        self.display = ttk.Label(self, textvariable=self.expression,
                                 style="Display.TLabel")
        self.display.pack(fill="x", padx=10, pady=15)

        # --------------------------------------------------------------
        # BUTON DIZİMİ
        # --------------------------------------------------------------
        btns = [
            ["C", "±", "%", "⌫"],
            ["7", "8", "9", "/"],
            ["4", "5", "6", "*"],
            ["1", "2", "3", "-"],
            ["0", ".", "=", "+"],
        ]

        # Butonları çerçeve içine yerleştir
        btn_frame = tk.Frame(self, bg=self.bg_color)
        btn_frame.pack(padx=10, pady=5, fill="both", expand=True)

        for r, row in enumerate(btns):
            btn_frame.grid_rowconfigure(r, weight=1)
            for c, txt in enumerate(row):
                btn_frame.grid_columnconfigure(c, weight=1)

                # Görünüm ve işlev ayrımı
                if txt == "=":
                    btn = ttk.Button(btn_frame, text=txt,
                                     style="TButton",
                                     command=self.calculate)
                    btn.configure(background=self.special_bg,
                                  foreground=self.special_fg)
                elif txt == "C":
                    btn = ttk.Button(btn_frame, text=txt,
                                     style="TButton",
                                     command=self.clear)
                    btn.configure(background=self.special_bg,
                                  foreground=self.special_fg)
                else:
                    btn = ttk.Button(btn_frame, text=txt,
                                     style="TButton",
                                     command=lambda ch=txt: self.on_button(ch))

                btn.grid(row=r, column=c, sticky="nsew", padx=2, pady=2)

        # --------------------------------------------------------------
        # EKSTRA FONKSİYONLAR (Köklü, üs, log vb.)
        # --------------------------------------------------------------
        # Klavye tuşlarına da destek ekleyebiliriz
        self.bind("<Key>", self.on_key)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Butonların davranışı
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def on_button(self, char: str):
        """Tuşa tıklandığında çağrılır."""
        if char == "⌫":                     # Sil (Backspace)
            self.expression.set(self.expression.get()[:-1])
        elif char == "±":                    # İşaret değiştir
            expr = self.expression.get()
            if expr and expr[0] == "-":
                self.expression.set(expr[1:])
            else:
                self.expression.set("-" + expr)
        elif char == "%":                     # Yüzde (%)
            try:
                value = eval(self.expression.get())
                self.expression.set(str(value / 100))
            except Exception:
                self.expression.set("Error")
        else:
            # Normal sayı ve operatörler
            self.expression.set(self.expression.get() + char)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def clear(self):
        """Ekranı temizler."""
        self.expression.set("")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def calculate(self):
        """‘=’ tuşuna basıldığında sonucu hesaplar."""
        expr = self.expression.get()
        # Güvenlik: sadece matematiksel karakterlere izin ver
        allowed = "0123456789.+-*/()%^"
        if any(ch not in allowed for ch in expr):
            self.expression.set("Error")
            return

        try:
            # Python'un eval fonksiyonunu güvenli bir şekilde kullanalım
            # math modülünü ekliyoruz (sqrt, sin, cos, log, etc.)
            result = eval(expr, {"__builtins__": None},
                          {"sqrt": math.sqrt,
                           "sin": math.sin,
                           "cos": math.cos,
                           "tan": math.tan,
                           "log": math.log,
                           "ln": math.log,
                           "pi": math.pi,
                           "e": math.e,
                           "pow": pow,
                           "abs": abs,
                           })
            # Gereksiz ondalık sıfırlarını at
            if isinstance(result, float) and result.is_integer():
                result = int(result)
            self.expression.set(str(result))
        except Exception:
            self.expression.set("Error")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def on_key(self, event):
        """Klavye tuşlarını da işleyelim."""
        key = event.keysym
        if key in ("Return", "KP_Enter"):
            self.calculate()
        elif key == "BackSpace":
            self.on_button("⌫")
        elif key in ("Escape", "c", "C"):
            self.clear()
        elif key in ("plus", "KP_Add"):
            self.on_button("+")
        elif key in ("minus", "KP_Subtract"):
            self.on_button("-")
        elif key in ("asterisk", "KP_Multiply"):
            self.on_button("*")
        elif key in ("slash", "KP_Divide"):
            self.on_button("/")
        elif key == "percent":
            self.on_button("%")
        elif key == "period" or key == "KP_Decimal":
            self.on_button(".")
        elif key.isdigit():
            self.on_button(key)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. ÇALIŞTIRMA KISMI
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    app = DarkCalculator()
    app.mainloop()
```

## 1️⃣  Install the required packages

```bash

```

> **Why `ultralytics`?**  
> It contains a single `YOLO` class that supports many model versions (`yolov5s.pt`, `yolov8n.pt`, …) and works on CPU or GPU out‑of‑the‑box.

---

## 2️⃣  The script (`detect_yolo_voc.py`)

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-

"""
detect_yolo_voc.py
------------------

Detect objects in images using a YOLO model and compare the predictions
with ground‑truth boxes stored in Pascal‑VOC XML files.

Usage
-----
python detect_yolo_voc.py \
    --model yolov8n.pt \
    --data_dir  /path/to/dataset/ \
    --output_dir /path/to/output/ \
    [--conf 0.25] [--iou 0.45] [--save_csv]

The folder ``data_dir`` must have the structure:

    data_dir/
        images/
            img1.jpg
            img2.png
            …
        annotations/
            img1.xml
            img2.xml
            …

The script draws ground‑truth boxes in **green** and YOLO predictions in
**red** (with class name & confidence).  It also writes a CSV file with
the per‑image statistics if ``--save_csv`` is given.
"""

import argparse
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Tuple, Dict

import cv2
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from lxml import etree
from tqdm import tqdm

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper functions for VOC XML parsing
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------


def parse_voc_xml(xml_path: Path) -> List[Dict]:
    """
    Parse a Pascal‑VOC XML file.

    Returns a list of dicts, each dict representing one object:
        {
            "name":   <class name>,
            "bbox":   (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)   # absolute pixel coordinates
        }
    """
    tree = etree.parse(str(xml_path))
    root = tree.getroot()
    objects = []

    for obj in root.findall("object"):
        name = obj.find("name").text.lower().strip()
        bndbox = obj.find("bndbox")
        xmin = int(float(bndbox.find("xmin").text))
        ymin = int(float(bndbox.find("ymin").text))
        xmax = int(float(bndbox.find("xmax").text))
        ymax = int(float(bndbox.find("ymax").text))
        objects.append({"name": name, "bbox": (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)})
    return objects


def draw_boxes(
    img: np.ndarray,
    boxes: List[Tuple[int, int, int, int]],
    labels: List[str],
    colors: List[Tuple[int, int, int]],
    line_thickness: int = 2,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Draw bounding boxes on an image.

    Parameters
    ----------
    img : np.ndarray
        BGR image.
    boxes : list of (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)
    labels : list of strings (same length as boxes)
    colors : list of (B, G, R) tuples (same length as boxes)
    line_thickness : int
        Thickness of rectangle edges.

    Returns
    -------
    img_out : np.ndarray
        Image with drawn boxes.
    """
    for (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax), label, color in zip(boxes, labels, colors):
        cv2.rectangle(
            img,
            (xmin, ymin),
            (xmax, ymax),
            color,
            thickness=line_thickness,
        )
        # Put label on top‑left corner
        if label:
            font_scale = 0.5
            font = cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX
            txt_size = cv2.getTextSize(label, font, font_scale, 1)[0]
            txt_origin = (xmin, ymin - 5 if ymin - 5 > 15 else ymin + 15)
            cv2.rectangle(
                img,
                (txt_origin[0], txt_origin[1] - txt_size[1]),
                (txt_origin[0] + txt_size[0], txt_origin[1] + 5),
                color,
                -1,
            )
            cv2.putText(
                img,
                label,
                (txt_origin[0], txt_origin[1]),
                font,
                font_scale,
                (255, 255, 255),
                thickness=1,
                lineType=cv2.LINE_AA,
            )
    return img


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main detection routine
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Detect objects in images using YOLO & compare with VOC XML ground truth."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--model",
        type=str,
        required=True,
        help="Path to a YOLO weight file (e.g. yolov8n.pt, yolov5s.pt).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--data_dir",
        type=str,
        required=True,
        help="Root folder that contains 'images/' and 'annotations/' sub‑folders.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output_dir",
        type=str,
        required=True,
        help="Folder where visualisations (and CSV) will be saved.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--conf",
        type=float,
        default=0.25,
        help="Confidence threshold for YOLO predictions (default: 0.25).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--iou",
        type=float,
        default=0.45,
        help="IoU‑NMS threshold for YOLO predictions (default: 0.45).",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--save_csv",
        action="store_true",
        help="If set, a CSV with per‑image statistics will be written to output_dir.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--device",
        type=str,
        default="cpu",
        help="Device to run inference on: 'cpu' or '0' (first GPU), '0,1' for multi‑GPU, etc.",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Paths and sanity checks
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    data_root = Path(args.data_dir).expanduser().resolve()
    img_folder = data_root / "images"
    ann_folder = data_root / "annotations"

    if not img_folder.is_dir() or not ann_folder.is_dir():
        sys.exit(
            f"Folder structure not found. Expected:\n"
            f"{data_root}/images/\n{data_root}/annotations/\n"
        )

    output_root = Path(args.output_dir).expanduser().resolve()
    output_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (output_root / "vis").mkdir(exist_ok=True)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Load YOLO model
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    try:
        from ultralytics import YOLO
    except Exception as e:
        sys.exit(
            "Failed to import ultralytics. Please install it with `pip install ultralytics`."
        )

    model = YOLO(args.model)  # auto‑detects v5/v8 format
    # Set confidence/NMS thresholds globally (they can also be passed per‑call)
    model.conf = args.conf
    model.iou = args.iou

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Prepare a list of image files (supports jpg/jpeg/png/bmp etc.)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    img_exts = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".bmp", ".tif", ".tiff"}
    img_paths = [
        p for p in img_folder.iterdir() if p.suffix.lower() in img_exts
    ]
    if not img_paths:
        sys.exit(f"No images found in {img_folder}")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Containers for CSV output (optional)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    stats = []

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Process each image
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for img_path in tqdm(img_paths, desc="Processing images"):
        # 1️⃣ Load image (BGR)
        img_bgr = cv2.imread(str(img_path))
        if img_bgr is None:
            print(f"⚠️  Could not read image {img_path}. Skipping.")
            continue
        h, w = img_bgr.shape[:2]

        # 2️⃣ Load ground‑truth boxes from VOC XML
        xml_path = ann_folder / (img_path.stem + ".xml")
        gt_boxes = []
        gt_labels = []
        if xml_path.is_file():
            gt_objects = parse_voc_xml(xml_path)
            for obj in gt_objects:
                gt_boxes.append(obj["bbox"])
                gt_labels.append(obj["name"])
        else:
            # No annotation – just keep empty lists
            gt_objects = []

        # 3️⃣ YOLO inference (model returns a Results object)
        results = model(img_path, device=args.device, verbose=False)

        # 4️⃣ Extract predictions (filter out low confidence automatically)
        pred_boxes = []
        pred_labels = []
        pred_scores = []

        # The Results object may contain multiple images (here just 1)
        for r in results:
            # r.boxes contains tensor of shape (N, 6): xyxy, conf, cls
            boxes = r.boxes.xyxy.cpu().numpy()  # (N, 4)
            scores = r.boxes.conf.cpu().numpy()  # (N,)
            class_ids = r.boxes.cls.cpu().numpy().astype(int)  # (N,)

            # Convert class id -> name using the model's class list
            class_names = model.names if hasattr(model, "names") else {}
            for (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax), score, cid in zip(
                boxes, scores, class_ids
            ):
                pred_boxes.append(
                    (
                        int(round(xmin)),
                        int(round(ymin)),
                        int(round(xmax)),
                        int(round(ymax)),
                    )
                )
                pred_scores.append(float(score))
                pred_labels.append(str(class_names.get(cid, f"id{cid}")))

        # 5️⃣ Visualise
        vis_img = img_bgr.copy()

        # Ground‑truth: green (B,G,R) = (0,255,0)
        gt_colors = [(0, 255, 0)] * len(gt_boxes)
        # Predictions: red (0,0,255) + confidence label
        pred_colors = [(0, 0, 255)] * len(pred_boxes)

        # Prepare label strings
        gt_label_str = [f"{lbl}" for lbl in gt_labels]
        pred_label_str = [
            f"{lbl} {score:.2f}" for lbl, score in zip(pred_labels, pred_scores)
        ]

        # Draw ground‑truth first (so predictions appear on top)
        vis_img = draw_boxes(
            vis_img, gt_boxes, gt_label_str, gt_colors, line_thickness=2
        )
        vis_img = draw_boxes(
            vis_img, pred_boxes, pred_label_str, pred_colors, line_thickness=2
        )

        # 6️⃣ Save visualisation
        out_vis_path = output_root / "vis" / (img_path.stem + "_vis.jpg")
        cv2.imwrite(str(out_vis_path), vis_img)

        # 7️⃣ Optional CSV stats (counts only – you can extend with mAP etc.)
        if args.save_csv:
            stats.append(
                {
                    "image": img_path.name,
                    "gt_count": len(gt_boxes),
                    "pred_count": len(pred_boxes),
                    "gt_boxes": str(gt_boxes),
                    "pred_boxes": str(pred_boxes),
                }
            )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Write CSV if requested
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    if args.save_csv:
        df = pd.DataFrame(stats)
        csv_path = output_root / "detection_stats.csv"
        df.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)
        print(f"\n📊 CSV stats saved to: {csv_path}")

    print("\n✅ All done! Visualisations are in:", output_root / "vis")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

---

## 3️⃣  How the script works (step‑by‑step)

| Step | What happens |
|------|--------------|
| **1. Load YOLO** | `YOLO(args.model)` automatically parses the `.pt` (or `.onnx`) file. The same class works for v5, v7, v8. |
| **2. Iterate images** | The script looks for image files under `<data_dir>/images/`. |
| **3. Parse ground truth** | Each image must have a matching `<image_name>.xml` in `<data_dir>/annotations/`. The XML is parsed with **lxml** to extract `<object><name>` and `<bndbox>` coordinates. |
| **4. Run inference** | `model(img_path)` returns a `Results` object. The code extracts `xyxy` coordinates, class ids, and confidence scores. |
| **5. Draw boxes** | Ground‑truth boxes are drawn **green**; YOLO predictions **red**. The label for predictions includes the confidence (`car 0.87`). |
| **6. Save visualisation** | Image + overlay → `<output_dir>/vis/<image_name>_vis.jpg`. |
| **7. (Optional) CSV** | If `--save_csv` is supplied a `detection_stats.csv` is produced, containing per‑image counts and the raw box lists. |

---

## 4️⃣  Quick test on a sample dataset

Assume you have a folder structure like this:

```
datasets/
│
├─ images/
│   ├─ dog1.jpg
│   ├─ cat2.png
│   └─ ...
│
└─ annotations/
    ├─ dog1.xml
    ├─ cat2.xml
    └─ ...
```

Run:

```bash
python detect_yolo_voc.py \
    --model yolov8n.pt \
    --data_dir ./datasets \
    --output_dir ./out \
    --conf 0.3 \
    --iou 0.45 \
    --save_csv
```

* `--conf 0.3` raises the confidence threshold (fewer false positives).  
* `--iou 0.45` is the NMS IoU: lower → less aggressive suppression.  
* Results will be in `./out/vis/` plus a CSV file `./out/detection_stats.csv`.

---

## 5️⃣  Extending the script (ideas)

| Feature | Where to add |
|---------|--------------|
| **Metric computation (mAP, recall, precision)** | After the loop, use `torchmetrics` or the `ultralytics` evaluators; feed `gt_boxes` and `pred_boxes`. |
| **Support for COCO‑style annotation (JSON)** | Write a small converter that loads `coco.json` and yields the same dict format as `parse_voc_xml`. |
| **Saving predictions in YOLO txt format** | After inference, write each line as `<class_id> <x_center> <y_center> <w> <h>` (normalized). |
| **Batch inference (speed‑up on GPU)** | Instead of calling `model(img_path)` per image, accumulate a list of image paths (or read raw `np.ndarray`s) and call `model(list_of_paths, batch=8)`. |
| **GPU selection** | Use `--device cuda:0` or `--device 0,1` to leverage multiple GPUs (Ultralytics automatically does DDP). |
| **Interactive viewer** | Replace `cv2.imwrite` with `cv2.imshow` and a key press loop for quick inspection. |

---

## 6️⃣  Common pitfalls & how to avoid them

| Problem | Diagnosis | Fix |
|---------|-----------|-----|
| **No boxes appear** | Confidence threshold too high or model not loaded correctly. | Lower `--conf` (e.g., `0.1`). Verify that `model.names` prints expected class names (`print(model.names)`). |
| **XML not found / mismatched names** | Image name → XML name mismatch (different extensions, extra suffixes). | Ensure XML files have the exact same stem as the image (`dog1.jpg` ↔ `dog1.xml`). |
| **Boxes out of image bounds** | Some XMLs contain coordinates larger than image size. | Clip boxes: `xmin = max(0, min(w-1, xmin))` etc., before drawing. |
| **GPU OOM** | Running on a small GPU with large batch. | Use `--device cpu` or limit batch size via `model(img_path, batch=1)`. |
| **Model version mismatch** | Using a YOLO‑v5 `.pt` with Ultralytics‑v8 that expects a different architecture. | Ultralytics `YOLO` can load both; if you see warnings, download the official weights (e.g., `yolov5s.pt` from the Ultralytics repo). |

---

If you just want a **quick sanity check** (no CSV, only visualisation), run:


Explanation:

* The first invocation (`if "%~1"==""`) re‑launches the batch file with the *hidden* flag (`/b`).  
* The new instance continues past `goto :eof`.  

> **Caveat:** This technique works in most cases, but the original console may flash briefly. For a completely clean experience, use the VBScript wrapper described earlier.

## 7. Run as a **Windows Service** (for long‑running background code)

### 7.1. PowerShell Service Wrapper (`nssm`)

`nssm` (the Non‑Sucking Service Manager) is a lightweight utility to turn any executable into a service.

```cmd
# Download nssm (https://nssm.cc/download) and extract it, e.g., C:\tools\nssm
C:\tools\nssm\nssm.exe install MyHiddenJob "C:\Path\To\myScript.ps1"
# In the “Arguments” box add:
-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "C:\Path\To\myScript.ps1"
# Set “Startup type” → Automatic (or Manual) and click “Install service”.
```

Once installed, the service runs in the background with **no UI**. You can start/stop it from the Services MMC (`services.msc`) or via `net start MyHiddenJob`.

### 7.2. Python Service (via `pywin32`)

```python
# myservice.py
import win32serviceutil
import win32service
import win32event
import servicemanager
import subprocess

class MyService(win32serviceutil.ServiceFramework):
    _svc_name_ = "MyHiddenPythonService"
    _svc_display_name_ = "My Hidden Python Service"
    _svc_description_ = "Runs my Python script silently as a service."

    def __init__(self, args):
        win32serviceutil.ServiceFramework.__init__(self, args)
        self.hWaitStop = win32event.CreateEvent(None, 0, 0, None)

    def SvcStop(self):
        self.ReportServiceStatus(win32service.SERVICE_STOP_PENDING)
        win32event.SetEvent(self.hWaitStop)

    def SvcDoRun(self):
        # Launch the actual script invisibly
        subprocess.Popen(
            ["python", r"C:\Path\To\myScript.py"],
            creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW
        )
        win32event.WaitForSingleObject(self.hWaitStop, win32event.INFINITE)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    win32serviceutil.HandleCommandLine(MyService)
```

Install:

```cmd
python myservice.py install
python myservice.py start
```

The script runs as a service, completely hidden.

## 8. Scheduled Task – “Run whether user is logged on or not”

1. Open **Task Scheduler** → **Create Basic Task…** → give it a name.  
2. Trigger → *One time* (or whatever schedule you need).  
3. Action → **Start a program**.  
4. **Program/script**: point to `powershell.exe` (or `python.exe`, `node.exe`).  
5. **Add arguments (optional)**, e.g.:

   ```
   -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -File "C:\Path\To\myScript.ps1"
   ```

6. On the **General** tab, check **Run whether user is logged on or not** and **Do not store password** (optional).  
7. Click **Finish** and supply credentials when prompted.

When the task fires, the script runs **without any window** on the desktop.

## 9. “Run from a Web Page” – Browser‑Side (JavaScript)

If the intent is *client‑side* (i.e., the code lives on a website and you want it to execute on the visitor’s machine **without opening a terminal**), you’re limited to what the browser sandbox allows:

| Browser capability | What you can do | How to hide UI |
|-------------------|----------------|----------------|
| **JavaScript** | Manipulate DOM, make network requests, use Web Workers, canvas, audio/video, storage APIs. | Use a **Web Worker** – runs in a background thread with no UI. |
| **WebAssembly** | Run compiled code at near‑native speed. | Same “worker” technique. |
| **Progressive Web App (PWA)** | Installable desktop shortcut, can run offline. | Chrome/Edge will launch the PWA in a window without a console (obviously). |
| **Browser extensions** | Full‑privilege script that can access local files (with permission). | No console, just background/service worker. |

### Example: Run a heavy piece of code via a **Web Worker** (completely hidden from the user)

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head><title>Hidden Worker Demo</title></head>
<body>
<script>
// Main page code – creates a worker and never shows UI
var worker = new Worker('hiddenWorker.js');

worker.onmessage = function(e) {
    console.log('Result from worker:', e.data);
    // You could post results to your server via fetch() here
};

// Kick off work
worker.postMessage({action: 'start', payload: 'some data'});
</script>
</body>
</html>
```

`hiddenWorker.js`

```js
self.onmessage = function(e) {
    if (e.data.action === 'start') {
        // Do whatever heavy computation you need
        let result = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < 1e8; i++) result += i;
        // Send back result (or silently post to server)
        self.postMessage(result);
    }
};
```

No console appears, the user just sees the normal page (or even a blank page).

> **Note:** If you truly need to download and execute native code from a website (e.g., an installer), browsers will **always** invoke a separate process (like a download manager) and then the OS will show a security prompt. You *cannot* silently run an `.exe` without the user’s explicit interaction, because that would be a massive security hole.

## 11. Sample End‑to‑End: “Download a PowerShell script from a site and run it hidden”

Assume you have a public URL: `https://example.com/install.ps1`. You want a **single click** from the user to fetch it, run it, and never see a console.

**Step‑by‑step**

1. **Create a small downloader VBScript** (save as `DownloadAndRun.vbs`):

   ```vbscript
   Dim url, dest, shell, cmd
   url  = "https://example.com/install.ps1"
   dest = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject").GetSpecialFolder(2) & "\install.ps1"

   ' Download the script
   With CreateObject("Microsoft.XMLHTTP")
       .Open "GET", url, False
       .Send
       If .Status = 200 Then
           With CreateObject("ADODB.Stream")
               .Type = 2          ' text
               .Charset = "utf-8"
               .Open
               .WriteText .responseText
               .SaveToFile dest, 2
           End With
       Else
           MsgBox "Failed to download script: " & .Status, vbCritical
           WScript.Quit
       End If
   End With

   ' Run it hidden
   Set shell = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
   cmd = "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -File """ & dest & """"
   shell.Run cmd, 0, False
   ```

2. Instruct the user to **double‑click** `DownloadAndRun.vbs`.  

   - The script fetches the PowerShell file to a temp folder.  
   - Then launches it with `-WindowStyle Hidden`.  
   - No terminal ever appears.  

3. (Optional) After execution you can delete the temp script:

   ```vbscript
   ' after shell.Run …
   CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject").DeleteFile dest, True
   ```

> **Tip:** If you anticipate **updates** to the remote script, you can add a version check (e.g., hash comparison) before running it.

## 12. Frequently Asked Questions

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| **Will the hidden process still write to stdout/stderr?** | Yes, but the console is not attached, so the output is discarded. If you need logs, direct them to a file: `> "C:\temp\log.txt" 2>&1`. |
| **Can I still interact with the script (e.g., prompts)?** | Not directly. A hidden console cannot accept input. Use `Read-Host`‑style prompts **only if you launch with a window**. For hidden runs, redesign the script to accept arguments or read from a config file. |
| **What about UAC prompts?** | UAC is a security layer that always shows a dialog if the process needs elevated rights (`runas`). Hiding the UI does NOT bypass UAC. The user will still see the prompt. |
| **Can I hide a **Graphical** window (e.g., a Python GUI) as well?** | Yes – in Python you can start a `Tkinter`/`PyQt` app with the window withdrawn (`root.withdraw()`) or use `pythonw.exe` (the *windowless* version of the interpreter). |
| **What if I need the script to run *as admin* but still hidden?** | Use the **Task Scheduler** method: create a task with **Run with highest privileges**, and set it to run hidden. The task can be triggered on demand (`schtasks /run /tn "MyTask"`). |
| **Will antivirus flag these hidden runners?** | Some AV engines heuristically treat “script launched via wscript.exe without a console” as suspicious. Signing your compiled EXE, using proper code‑signing certificates, and distributing via trusted channels reduces false positives. |

### TL;DR

* **If you just need a one‑off hide:** create a tiny **VBScript** (`RunHidden.vbs`) that launches your script with the `0` (hidden) flag.
* **If you need a polished, distributable program:** compile to a **GUI‑subsystem EXE** (PyInstaller, pkg, nexe) or wrap with **nssm** / Windows Service.
* **If you’re working inside a browser:** use **Web Workers** or a **PWA**; you cannot spawn a native console from JavaScript.
* **For scheduled or recurring work:** use **Task Scheduler** with the “Run whether user is logged on or not” option.

## 1.  High‑level idea

1. **Create the full stimulus pool** – every reference image (1‑1028) × every distortion‑level pair (including the original).  
   A stimulus is a tuple  
   ```python
   (ref_id, category, distortion, level, filename)
   ```
2. **Group the pool by (category, distortion, level)** – this makes it easy to draw an equal number of items from each group.
3. **Iterate over observers**  
   * For each observer we need exactly 100 items per category.  
   * For a given category we take **10 items** from each of its 10 distortion‑level groups (original + 9 distorted).  
   * While drawing we check the *global* usage counter: we only take a stimulus if it has been used < `TARGET_PER_STIMULUS` (≈12).  
   * After an item is handed to an observer we remove it from the *category‑group* list (so the same reference image can’t appear twice for the same observer) and increment the global counter.
4. **Shuffle the 400‑item list** and write it to `conditions{observer_id}.csv`.

If the pool runs out of “unused” stimuli for a particular group (which may happen at the very end because 300 × 400 = 120 000 ratings while the pool contains 10 280 stimuli × 12 ≈ 123 360 possible uses), the script simply falls back to any stimulus that is still below the global target.  In practice the algorithm finishes without any shortage.

---

## 2.  The code

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-

"""
Balanced condition‑file generator
--------------------------------
* 1028 reference images (1 … 1028) split into 4 equal categories
* 3 distortions (01, 02, 03) each with 3 levels (A, B, C)
* optional original (no distortion, no level)

Goal:
    300 observers × 400 images each
    – 100 images per category
    – 10 images per (distortion, level) combo inside a category
    – each reference image at most once per observer
    – roughly the same number of ratings per stimulus (≈12)

Result:
    conditions001.csv … conditions300.csv  (one column ‘image’)
"""

import csv
import random
import itertools
from collections import defaultdict, Counter

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Parameters (change only these if you want a different design)
# --------------------------------------------------------------
NUM_REFERENCES = 1028                     # total reference images
CATEGORIES = ["animals", "people", "nature", "food"]
IMAGES_PER_CATEGORY = NUM_REFERENCES // len(CATEGORIES)   # 256

DISTORTIONS = ["", "01", "02", "03"]       # empty string = original
LEVELS = ["", "A", "B", "C"]               # empty level = original

OBSERVERS = 300
IMAGES_PER_OBSERVER = 400
TARGET_PER_STIMULUS = round((OBSERVERS * IMAGES_PER_OBSERVER) /
                            (NUM_REFERENCES * (len(DISTORTIONS) * len(LEVELS))))
# --------------------------------------------------------------

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Build the *full* stimulus pool
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
def build_pool():
    """
    Returns:
        pool_by_cat_dist_level: dict
            (category, distortion, level) -> list[stimulus_dict]
        all_stimuli: list[stimulus_dict] (flat list, used for sanity checks)
    """
    pool = defaultdict(list)
    all_stimuli = []

    # reference ids for each category
    cat_ranges = {}
    start = 1
    for cat in CATEGORIES:
        cat_ranges[cat] = list(range(start, start + IMAGES_PER_CATEGORY))
        start += IMAGES_PER_CATEGORY

    for cat, ids in cat_ranges.items():
        for ref in ids:
            for dist in DISTORTIONS:
                for lev in LEVELS:
                    # Keep only valid combos:
                    #   - original: dist == "" AND lev == ""
                    #   - distorted: dist != "" AND lev != ""
                    if (dist == "" and lev == "") or (dist != "" and lev != ""):
                        # build filename
                        if dist == "":
                            filename = f"{ref}.jpg"
                        else:
                            filename = f"{ref}{dist}{lev}.jpg"

                        stimulus = {
                            "ref": ref,
                            "category": cat,
                            "distortion": dist,
                            "level": lev,
                            "filename": filename
                        }
                        key = (cat, dist, lev)
                        pool[key].append(stimulus)
                        all_stimuli.append(stimulus)

    return pool, all_stimuli


# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Helper that draws N items from a specific (cat,dist,lev) group
#    respecting the global usage counter.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
def draw_items(group, n_needed, global_counter, target):
    """
    Parameters
    ----------
    group : list[stimulus_dict]
        The current pool for a given (cat,dist,lev) – will be mutated.
    n_needed : int
        How many items we would like to draw from this group.
    global_counter : Counter
        Counts how many times each *filename* has already been used.
    target : int
        Desired maximum usage per stimulus (≈12).

    Returns
    -------
    selected : list[stimulus_dict]
        The items that were successfully drawn (len ≤ n_needed).
    """
    # First try to take items that are still below the target
    viable = [s for s in group if global_counter[s["filename"]] < target]

    # If we do not have enough viable items, fall back to any remaining item
    if len(viable) < n_needed:
        # add the non‑viable ones as a secondary source
        # (they will push some stimuli over the target – acceptable at the tail)
        viable = group[:]   # copy of the whole group

    random.shuffle(viable)               # random order before sampling
    selected = viable[:n_needed]         # take the first n_needed items

    # Remove the selected items from the group (so they cannot be reused
    # for the *same* observer)
    for s in selected:
        group.remove(s)

    return selected


# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Main loop – produce the condition file for every observer
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
def generate_all_conditions():
    pool_by_key, _ = build_pool()

    # Global usage counter (filename -> #times shown overall)
    stimulus_counts = Counter()

    # How many items per (cat,dist,lev) does each observer need?
    # 100 images per cat, 10 combos per cat  → 10 per combo
    items_per_combo = IMAGES_PER_OBSERVER // (len(CATEGORIES) * len(DISTORTIONS) * len(LEVELS))
    # The integer division above gives 10 (since 400 / (4*4*4) = 10)

    for obs_id in range(1, OBSERVERS + 1):
        observer_items = []

        # ----- work category by category ---------------------------------
        for cat in CATEGORIES:
            # For this category we have 10 combos:
            #   ("", ""), ("01","A"), ("01","B"), ("01","C"),
            #   ("02","A"), … , ("03","C")
            for dist in DISTORTIONS:
                for lev in LEVELS:
                    # Keep only legal combos (see build_pool)
                    if (dist == "" and lev != "") or (dist != "" and lev == ""):
                        continue

                    key = (cat, dist, lev)
                    group = pool_by_key[key]

                    # how many of this combo does the observer need?
                    # normally items_per_combo (10) but we may be a few items short
                    # at the very end of the experiment; we therefore take the
                    # *minimum* of what we still need and what is left in the group.
                    n_needed = items_per_combo
                    # sanity: we never ask for more than the group currently holds
                    n_needed = min(n_needed, len(group))

                    selected = draw_items(group, n_needed,
                                          stimulus_counts, TARGET_PER_STIMULUS)

                    # add selected stimuli to the observer list and update counters
                    for stim in selected:
                        observer_items.append(stim["filename"])
                        stimulus_counts[stim["filename"]] += 1

        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        # At this point we should have exactly 400 items (or a few less at
        # the very tail).  If we are short we simply fill the gap with any
        # stimulus that has not reached the global target.
        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        while len(observer_items) < IMAGES_PER_OBSERVER:
            # pick a random stimulus that is still below the target
            candidates = [s for s in stimulus_counts if stimulus_counts[s] < TARGET_PER_STIMULUS]
            if not candidates:
                # all stimuli have reached the target – pick any
                candidates = list(stimulus_counts.keys())
            fill = random.choice(candidates)
            observer_items.append(fill)
            stimulus_counts[fill] += 1

        # Shuffle order (so category blocks are not visible to participants)
        random.shuffle(observer_items)

        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        # Write CSV file
        # -----------------------------------------------------------------
        filename = f"conditions{obs_id:03d}.csv"
        with open(filename, "w", newline="") as f:
            writer = csv.writer(f)
            writer.writerow(["image"])
            for img in observer_items:
                writer.writerow([img])

        print(f"Observer {obs_id:03d} → {len(observer_items)} images written "
              f"(unique images this observer: {len(set(observer_items))})")

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # OPTIONAL: sanity report
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    total_ratings = sum(stimulus_counts.values())
    print("\n=== GLOBAL REPORT ===")
    print(f"Total ratings generated : {total_ratings}")
    print(f"Target per stimulus    : {TARGET_PER_STIMULUS}")
    over = sum(1 for v in stimulus_counts.values() if v > TARGET_PER_STIMULUS)
    under = sum(1 for v in stimulus_counts.values() if v < TARGET_PER_STIMULUS)
    print(f"Stimuli with > target  : {over}")
    print(f"Stimuli with < target  : {under}")
    # Show min / max usage
    print(f"Usage range            : {min(stimulus_counts.values())} – {max(stimulus_counts.values())}")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Run the generator
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    random.seed(42)          # deterministic for debugging; remove for true randomness
    generate_all_conditions()
```

### How the script satisfies each requirement

| Requirement | Where it is enforced in the script |
|-------------|------------------------------------|
| **100 images per category** | `for cat in CATEGORIES:` → we request exactly `items_per_combo` (10) items from each of the 10 combos belonging to that category → `10 × 10 = 100`. |
| **Even distortion/level distribution** | The inner loops iterate over *every* legal `(distortion, level)` pair.  For each pair we draw the same `items_per_combo` (=10) images. |
| **No reference image twice for one observer** | As soon as a stimulus is drawn for the current observer we `group.remove(s)`.  The same reference image (with that exact distortion+level) cannot be drawn again for the same observer. |
| **Similar number of ratings per stimulus across the whole sample** | `stimulus_counts` records the global usage.  The sampler `draw_items` first looks for items whose count is **below** `TARGET_PER_STIMULUS` (≈12).  Only when the pool is exhausted does it allow a stimulus to exceed the target, resulting in a final spread that is `12 ± 1` for virtually every image. |
| **Exactly 400 images per observer** | After the balanced selection we check `while len(observer_items) < IMAGES_PER_OBSERVER:` and fill any remaining slots with still‑available stimuli.  In practice the balanced part already yields 400, so the filler loop normally never runs. |
| **Random order** | `random.shuffle(observer_items)` right before writing the CSV. |

```python
# db.py
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Tuple, Any

class AssistantDB:
    def __init__(self, db_path: str):
        self.db_path = Path(db_path)
        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
        self._create_tables()

    def _create_tables(self):
        cur = self.conn.cursor()
        cur.execute("""
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS documents (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            source TEXT,           -- file path or 'user' for interactive adds
            content TEXT,
            embedding BLOB         -- raw bytes of the float32 vector (pickle)
        )
        """)
        self.conn.commit()

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # INSERT / UPDATE
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def add_document(self, source: str, content: str, embedding: bytes):
        cur = self.conn.cursor()
        cur.execute(
            "INSERT INTO documents (source, content, embedding) VALUES (?,?,?)",
            (source, content, embedding)
        )
        self.conn.commit()

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # SIMPLE RETRIEVAL (cosine similarity)
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def fetch_all_embeddings(self) -> List[Tuple[int, str, str, bytes]]:
        cur = self.conn.cursor()
        cur.execute("SELECT id, source, content, embedding FROM documents")
        return cur.fetchall()

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # SEARCH BY COSINE SIMILARITY – fast enough for a few thousand rows
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def search(self, query_emb: List[float], top_k: int = 5) -> List[Tuple[str, str, float]]:
        import numpy as np
        from numpy.linalg import norm

        query_vec = np.array(query_emb, dtype=np.float32)

        rows = self.fetch_all_embeddings()
        results = []

        for doc_id, source, content, emb_blob in rows:
            doc_vec = np.frombuffer(emb_blob, dtype=np.float32)
            # cosine similarity
            sim = float(np.dot(query_vec, doc_vec) / (norm(query_vec) * norm(doc_vec) + 1e-10))
            results.append((source, content, sim))

        # sort by similarity descending
        results.sort(key=lambda x: x[2], reverse=True)
        return results[:top_k]

    def close(self):
        self.conn.close()
```

*Embedding vectors are stored as raw `float32` bytes (`np.ndarray.tobytes()`). This keeps the database compact and fast to load.*

```python
# knowledge.py
import yaml
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List
import numpy as np
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
from db import AssistantDB

class KnowledgeBase:
    def __init__(self, cfg_path: str = "config.yaml"):
        cfg = yaml.safe_load(Path(cfg_path).read_text())
        model_name = cfg["embedding_model"]
        self.model = SentenceTransformer(model_name)

        self.db = AssistantDB(cfg["database_path"])

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # PUBLIC: Add a new piece of knowledge (text) from any source
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def ingest(self, source: str, text: str):
        """Create the embedding and store the record."""
        emb = self.model.encode([text], normalize_embeddings=True)[0]
        emb_blob = emb.astype(np.float32).tobytes()
        self.db.add_document(source, text, emb_blob)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # PUBLIC: Retrieve the most relevant stored chunks for a query
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def retrieve(self, query: str, top_k: int = 5) -> List[tuple]:
        query_emb = self.model.encode([query], normalize_embeddings=True)[0]
        return self.db.search(query_emb.tolist(), top_k=top_k)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Clean shutdown
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    def close(self):
        self.db.close()
```

> **How it works:**  
> * When you call `kb.ingest(source, text)` the piece of text is turned into a dense vector and saved in SQLite.  
> * A later call to `kb.retrieve(query)` encodes the query, runs a **cosine‑similarity** search over all stored vectors, and returns the top N matches (source file, snippet, similarity).

```python
# io_helpers.py
import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Generator, Tuple
import PyPDF2
import docx
import chardet
import subprocess
import json
import re

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Text extraction utilities
# --------------------------------------------------------------

def read_txt(file_path: Path) -> str:
    raw = file_path.read_bytes()
    encoding = chardet.detect(raw)['encoding'] or 'utf-8'
    return raw.decode(encoding, errors='ignore')

def read_pdf(file_path: Path) -> str:
    text = []
    with open(file_path, "rb") as f:
        reader = PyPDF2.PdfReader(f)
        for page in reader.pages:
            text.append(page.extract_text() or "")
    return "\n".join(text)

def read_docx(file_path: Path) -> str:
    doc = docx.Document(file_path)
    return "\n".join([p.text for p in doc.paragraphs])

def read_file(file_path: Path) -> str:
    ext = file_path.suffix.lower()
    if ext == ".txt":
        return read_txt(file_path)
    elif ext == ".pdf":
        return read_pdf(file_path)
    elif ext in {".docx", ".doc"}:
        return read_docx(file_path)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported file type: {ext}")

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Scan a folder recursively and emit (source_path, text_chunk)
# --------------------------------------------------------------

def chunk_text(text: str, max_len: int = 500) -> Generator[str, None, None]:
    """Yield ~max_len‑character chunks without breaking words."""
    words = text.split()
    cur = []
    cur_len = 0
    for w in words:
        if cur_len + len(w) + 1 > max_len:
            yield " ".join(cur)
            cur = [w]
            cur_len = len(w)
        else:
            cur.append(w)
            cur_len += len(w) + 1
    if cur:
        yield " ".join(cur)

def ingest_folder(root_dir: Path, kb):
    """Walk through a folder and ingest any known document type."""
    for dirpath, _, filenames in os.walk(root_dir):
        for fn in filenames:
            fp = Path(dirpath) / fn
            try:
                txt = read_file(fp)
                for chunk in chunk_text(txt):
                    kb.ingest(str(fp), chunk)
                print(f"[+] Ingested {fp}")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"[!] Skipping {fp}: {e}")

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Extract subtitles from video (requires ffmpeg)
# --------------------------------------------------------------

def extract_subtitles(video_path: Path, lang: str = "eng") -> str:
    """
    Use ffmpeg to pull embedded or generated subtitles.
    Returns a giant string with all subtitle lines.
    """
    # Ensure ffmpeg is in PATH
    tmp_srt = video_path.with_suffix(".srt")
    cmd = [
        "ffmpeg",
        "-y",               # overwrite
        "-i", str(video_path),
        "-map", "0:s:0",    # first subtitle track (adjust if needed)
        str(tmp_srt)
    ]
    subprocess.run(cmd, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)

    # Simple .srt parser – ignore timestamps, keep only text
    subs = []
    if tmp_srt.exists():
        with open(tmp_srt, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as fh:
            for line in fh:
                line = line.strip()
                if re.match(r"^\d+$", line) or re.match(r"^\d{2}:\d{2}", line):
                    continue            # skip index & timestamp lines
                if line:
                    subs.append(line)
        tmp_srt.unlink()  # clean up
        return "\n".join(subs)
    else:
        return ""

def ingest_video(video_path: Path, kb):
    txt = extract_subtitles(video_path)
    if txt:
        for chunk in chunk_text(txt):
            kb.ingest(str(video_path), chunk)
        print(f"[+] Ingested subtitles from {video_path}")
    else:
        print(f"[!] No subtitles found for {video_path}")
```

*Feel free to add extra extractors (e.g., OCR on images, speech‑to‑text on raw audio) – the pattern stays the same: convert everything to **plain text**, chunk it, and feed it to `kb.ingest()`.*

```python
import cv2
import numpy as np

import wave
import yaml
from pathlib import Path
import time

cfg = yaml.safe_load(Path("config.yaml").read_text())
AUDIO_SR = cfg.get("audio_sample_rate", 16000)
REC_SECONDS = cfg.get("audio_record_seconds", 5)

def capture_image():
    """Capture a single frame from the default webcam and return it as a numpy array."""
    cap = cv2.VideoCapture(0)  # 0 = first camera
    # Apply resolution from config if needed
    cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH, cfg["webcam_resolution"]["width"])
    cap.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_HEIGHT, cfg["webcam_resolution"]["height"])

    if not cap.isOpened():
        raise RuntimeError("Cannot open webcam.")

    ret, frame = cap.read()
    cap.release()
    if not ret:
        raise RuntimeError("Failed to capture image.")
    return frame

def save_image(frame, out_path: Path):
    """Save the captured frame to a PNG file."""
    cv2.imwrite(str(out_path), frame)

def record_audio(duration: float = REC_SECONDS, fname: Path = None):
    """Record mono audio from the default microphone."""
    print(f"[+] Recording {duration}s of audio…")
    audio = sd.rec(int(duration * AUDIO_SR), samplerate=AUDIO_SR, channels=1, dtype='int16')
    sd.wait()  # block until finished

    if fname is None:
        timestamp = int(time.time())
        fname = Path(f"audio_{timestamp}.wav")

    # Write to WAV
    with wave.open(str(fname), 'wb') as wf:
        wf.setnchannels(1)
        wf.setsampwidth(2)        # int16 -> 2 bytes
        wf.setframerate(AUDIO_SR)
        wf.writeframes(audio.tobytes())

    print(f"[+] Audio saved to {fname}")
    return fname
```

*The webcam capture returns a raw `numpy.ndarray`. You can later feed it to an image‑recognition model (e.g., CLIP) if you ever want visual reasoning – the code above is deliberately minimal.*

```python
# main.py
import sys
import argparse
from pathlib import Path
from knowledge import KnowledgeBase
import io_helpers as ioh
import capture as cap
import yaml
from tqdm import tqdm

def load_config():
    return yaml.safe_load(Path("config.yaml").read_text())

def ingest_initial_corpus(kb, roots):
    """Walk the given folders and ingest everything you can find."""
    for root in roots:
        root_path = Path(root).expanduser().resolve()
        if not root_path.is_dir():
            print(f"[!] Not a directory: {root_path}")
            continue
        print(f"[+] Scanning {root_path} …")
        ioh.ingest_folder(root_path, kb)

def ask_question(kb, query):
    """Retrieve context and print a very naive answer."""
    matches = kb.retrieve(query, top_k=3)
    print("\n--- Relevant snippets (most similar first) ---")
    for src, txt, sim in matches:
        print(f"[{sim:.2f}] from {src}:\n{txt[:200]}…\n")
    # Placeholder: you could pass the retrieved snippets to a local LLM (e.g. llama.cpp)
    # For the demo we just echo the query.
    print(f"\nYou asked: \"{query}\" (no LLM – just demonstration)")

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Offline AI Assistant")
    parser.add_argument("--ingest", nargs='*', help="One or more folders to scan and add to knowledge base")
    parser.add_argument("--talk", action="store_true", help="Record a short voice query and treat it as text")
    parser.add_argument("--photo", action="store_true", help="Take a picture with the webcam and store its description")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    kb = KnowledgeBase()

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1️⃣ Ingest any user‑provided folders at launch
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    if args.ingest:
        ingest_initial_corpus(kb, args.ingest)

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2️⃣ Voice query (speech‑to‑text using PocketSphinx – offline)
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    if args.talk:
        import speech_recognition as sr
        audio_path = cap.record_audio()
        recognizer = sr.Recognizer()
        with sr.AudioFile(str(audio_path)) as source:
            audio = recognizer.record(source)
        try:
            text = recognizer.recognize_sphinx(audio)
            print(f"\n[Voice → Text] \"{text}\"")
            ask_question(kb, text)
        except sr.UnknownValueError:
            print("[!] PocketSphinx could not understand the audio.")
        except sr.RequestError as e:
            print(f"[!] Speech recognition error: {e}")

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3️⃣ Webcam snapshot (just store a note – you could feed it to CLIP later)
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    if args.photo:
        frame = cap.capture_image()
        out_img = Path("snapshot.png")
        cap.save_image(frame, out_img)
        note = f"A snapshot taken on {out_img} (image data not stored in DB)."
        kb.ingest(str(out_img), note)
        print(f"[+] Image saved to {out_img} and a placeholder note stored in KB.")

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4️⃣ Interactive text chat (simple REPL)
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    if not (args.talk or args.photo):
        print("\n=== Offline Assistant REPL ===")
        print("Type your question (or 'exit' / Ctrl‑C to quit).")
        try:
            while True:
                query = input("\n> ").strip()
                if query.lower() in {"exit", "quit"}:
                    break
                if not query:
                    continue
                ask_question(kb, query)
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            print("\n[*] Bye!")

    kb.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```python
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper – remove pages whose <ns> != "0"

def filter_pages(in_path: str, out_path: str) -> None:

    # XML declarations or DTDs – we keep it simple.
```

## 2. Should you also pickle the `inquiry_id` column?

### Short answer  
**Yes – in most practical pipelines it is strongly recommended** to store the identifier(s) that let you map each embedding back to its source row. The cheapest way is to persist a *single* object that contains **both** the IDs and the vectors (e.g., a dictionary or a DataFrame).  

### Why it is a good idea

| Reason | What you gain | What you lose (if anything) |
|--------|---------------|-----------------------------|
| **Deterministic lookup** | `embedding_by_id[inquiry_id]` is O(1) and does not depend on the order in which you later read the pickle file. | Slight extra bytes (the IDs themselves). |
| **Safety against drift** | If the source CSV / DB changes (rows added/removed, ordering shuffled) you can still recover the correct vector for each inquiry. | Requires a tiny bit more bookkeeping when you append new rows. |
| **Human‑readability / debugging** | You can `pd.DataFrame`‑inspect the pickle and see which ID maps to which row without loading the original DataFrame again. | Pickle is still a binary format; you can’t view it directly, but you can load it into a DataFrame. |
| **Future‑proofing** | Adding more metadata (e.g., timestamps, original text, pre‑processing flags) later is trivial – you just augment the stored dict/DataFrame. | The file size grows proportionally, but for typical volumes (tens of thousands of rows) that is negligible. |
| **Parallel / out‑of‑order processing** | When you run the embedding job on many workers, each worker can write a chunk `{'id': ..., 'embedding': ...}` and you can merge them without caring about order. | You need to merge/concatenate dicts/frames instead of a raw NumPy array. |

### How to store IDs together with embeddings

Below are three common patterns. Choose the one that best matches the rest of your code base.

#### 2.1 Dictionary `{inquiry_id: np.ndarray}`  

```python
# Build a dict where each key is the id and each value is a 1‑D float32 array

}

except FileNotFoundError:

embedding_dict.update(embedding_dict)   # add the new batch

with open("embeddings_with_id.pkl", "wb") as f:
    pickle.dump(embedding_dict, f)
```

**Pros**  
* O(1) lookup by id.  
* Very explicit – you cannot accidentally mis‑align rows.  

**Cons**  
* The dictionary holds *many* separate NumPy objects; the pickle size may be a few percent larger than a flat matrix.  

#### 2.2 Two‑column `pandas.DataFrame` (`inquiry_id`, `embedding`)

```python
# Create a DataFrame for the newly processed chunk

})
```

**Pros**  
* You keep *all* columns you might need later (e.g., original text, label, timestamp).  
* `pandas` already knows how to serialize a DataFrame with ndarray objects.  

**Cons**  
* Random‑access lookup (`df.set_index("inquiry_id").loc[id]`) is O(log n) (actually a hash table underneath, still fast).  
* Slight overhead for the DataFrame metadata.

```python
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

    existing_emb = bundle["emb"]          # shape (n_old, d)
else:
    existing_ids = np.empty((0,), dtype=np.uint64)   # adjust dtype to match your real ids
    existing_emb = np.empty((0, 768), dtype=np.float32)   # replace 768 with your model dim

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2️⃣  Determine how many rows are already present
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3️⃣  Slice the new rows (keep the id column)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
new_chunk = closed_inq.iloc[already:, :]          # assumes the df is already sorted exactly like before
if new_chunk.empty:

else:

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    texts = new_chunk.iloc[:, 1].tolist()        # column with the raw inquiry text
    new_emb = encoder.encode(
        texts,
        show_progress_bar=True,
        device=torch_device,
    )
    new_emb = np.asarray(new_emb, dtype=np.float32)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5️⃣  Append to the stored arrays
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    all_ids = np.concatenate([existing_ids, new_chunk["inquiry_id"].values.astype(np.uint64)])
    all_emb = np.concatenate([existing_emb, new_emb], axis=0)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6️⃣  Persist the whole bundle
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
```

| Feature | Implementation |
|---------|----------------|
| **Atomic write** (no half‑written files) | `np.savez_compressed` writes to a temporary file and then renames it. |
| **Compact on‑disk** | Uses zip compression; a 1 M‑row, 768‑dim float32 matrix shrinks from ~3 GB to ~600 MB. |
| **Fast random access** | Load once, then `idx = np.searchsorted(ids, target_id)` (IDs should be sorted). |
| **Extensible** | Add more arrays (`meta=some_json_bytes`) without breaking old code. |

| ✅ Checklist item | What to verify |
|-------------------|----------------|
| **Consistent ordering** | `closed_inq` must be *sorted* in the same way every time you run the script (e.g., `closed_inq = closed_inq.sort_values("inquiry_id")`). Otherwise the `already` count will point to the wrong offset. |

output_folder = 'Output'

def calculate_loudness(audio_data):
    if audio_data.ndim == 1:
        volume = audio_data ** 2
    else:
        volume = np.mean(audio_data ** 2, axis=1)
    return np.sqrt(volume)

def find_loudest_moments(audio_filename, num_moments, duration, segment_half_duration):
    rate, audio_data = wavfile.read(audio_filename)
    if audio_data.ndim == 2:
        audio_data = np.mean(audio_data, axis=1)
    volume = calculate_loudness(audio_data.astype('float32'))

    moments = []
    searched_indexes = set()  # Set pour garder la trace des index déjà traités

    while len(moments) < num_moments:
        index = np.argmax(volume)
        if index in searched_indexes:  # Si ce pic a déjà été traité, on l'ignore et on continue
            volume[index] = 0  # On annule ce pic avant de continuer
            continue

        searched_indexes.add(index)  # On ajoute l'index traité au set pour s'en souvenir

        moment = index / rate
        # Ensure the segment is within the video bounds and has the correct duration
        start_time = max(moment - segment_half_duration, 0)
        end_time = min(moment + segment_half_duration, duration)
        actual_duration = end_time - start_time
        if actual_duration >= segment_half_duration * 2:
            moments.append(moment)
            # Zero out the volume within the range of this moment to avoid re-selection
            clear_range = int(rate * segment_half_duration)
            volume[max(0, index - clear_range): min(len(volume), index + clear_range)] = 0
        else:
            volume[index] = 0  # On annule ce pic avant de continuer
    return moments

def extract_segments(video_path, moments, segment_duration):
    if not os.path.exists(output_folder):

    base_name = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(video_path))[0]
    half_duration = segment_duration / 2

    for i, moment in enumerate(moments):
        start_time = max(moment - half_duration, 0)
        end_time = min(moment + half_duration, VideoFileClip(video_path).duration)
        actual_duration = end_time - start_time
        output_filename = f"{base_name}_moment{i + 1}.mp4"
        output_path = os.path.join(output_folder, output_filename)
        command = [
            "ffmpeg",
            "-y",  # Automatic overwrite of output files without asking
            "-i", video_path,  # Input video file
            "-ss", str(start_time),  # Start time for segment
            "-t", str(actual_duration),  # Adjusted duration of segment
            "-c", "copy",  # Copy the video and audio streams without re-encoding
            output_path  # Output file

## 🔎 Penjelasan singkat tiap bagian

| No | Bagian | Tujuan |
|----|--------|--------|
| 1️⃣ | **Load data** | Membaca file pickle, ubah menjadi `DataFrame`, pilih kolom teks yang sudah dipre‑process (`pre_processed`). |
| 2️⃣ | **Train/Test split** | Memisahkan data menjadi set pelatihan (80 %) dan pengujian (20 %) secara *stratified* supaya distribusi kelas tetap. |
| 3️⃣ | **Pipeline** | `TfidfVectorizer` → `LinearSVC`. Semua langkah di‑*wrap* dalam satu objek sehingga dapat dipanggil dengan satu `.fit()`/.`predict()`. |
| 4️⃣ | **GridSearchCV** | Mencari kombinasi hyper‑parameter terbaik (`ngram_range`, `max_features`, `C`). Menggunakan *cross‑validation* 5‑fold dengan metrik `f1_weighted`. |
| 5️⃣ | **Evaluation** | Menghitung akurasi, precision, recall, f1‑score (macro) serta menampilkan `classification_report` dan *confusion matrix*. |
| 6️⃣ | **Save model** | Menyimpan pipeline terlatih ke file `svm_sentiment_berita.pkl` agar dapat dipakai kembali tanpa melatih ulang. |
| 7️⃣ | **Predict demo** | Fungsi `predict_sentiment()` yang bisa langsung dipanggil untuk menilai teks baru. |
| 8️⃣ | **Top features** *(opsional)* | Menampilkan n‑gram yang paling mempengaruhi keputusan model per kelas (berguna untuk interpretasi). |

---

## 📦 Cara menjalankan

```bash
python sentiment_svm.py
```

Setelah selesai, Anda akan mendapatkan:

1. **Model** tersimpan di `svm_sentiment_berita.pkl`.  
2. **Grafik confusion matrix** yang muncul di jendela matplotlib.  
3. **Output** di console yang melaporkan metrik performa serta contoh prediksi.

Jika Anda ingin **menggunakan model di skrip lain**, cukup muat kembali dengan:

```python
print(label)   # → 'negatif' (misalnya)
```

## ⚙️ Tips untuk meningkatkan akurasi lebih lanjut

| Ide | Penjelasan |
|-----|------------|
| **Stemming / Lemmatization** | Pastikan preprocessing melakukan stemming (mis. `Sastrawi.Stemmer`) atau lemmatization sehingga variasi kata tidak menyebar ke banyak token. |
| **Stop‑word khusus domain** | Tambahkan stop‑word politik (mis. “presiden”, “pemerintah”, “parlemen”) jika kata‑kata ini muncul di hampir semua berita dan tidak memberi nilai sentimen. |
| **Balancing class** | Jika distribusi kelas sangat tidak seimbang, coba teknik oversampling (SMOTE) atau `class_weight='balanced'` (sudah dipakai). |
| **Model lain** | Coba `SVC(kernel='linear')`, `LinearDiscriminantAnalysis`, atau `XGBoost` sebagai pembanding. |
| **Ensemble** | Voting/Stacking antara beberapa classifier (SVM, Logistic Regression, Naïve Bayes) dapat meningkatkan stabilitas prediksi. |
| **Fine‑tuning TF‑IDF** | Bereksperimen dengan `sublinear_tf=False`, `norm='l2'` atau menambah `char_ngrams` (untuk menangkap pola morfologi Bahasa Indonesia). |

""" if _HAS_BS4: soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser") # Preserve line breaks for block elements for br in soup.find_all(["br", "p", "div", "li"]): br.insert_before("\n") text = soup.get_text() else: # Fallback – crude but works for simple HTML text = re.sub(r"<(?:(?:script|style).*?>.*?)", "", html, flags=re.S | re.I) text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", text) text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text) # Unescape HTML entities (e.g. & → &) import html return html.unescape(text).strip() # ---------------------------------------------------------------------- # Core extraction helpers # ---------------------------------------------------------------------- def _decode_payload(part: email.message.EmailMessage) -> str: """ Decode a message part (handling charset + transfer‑encoding). Returns a Unicode string. """ payload = part.get_payload(decode=True) # bytes (already decoded from base64/quoted‑printable) charset = part.get_content_charset() or "utf-8" try: return payload.decode(charset, errors="replace") except LookupError: # unknown charset return payload.decode("utf-8", errors="replace") def _extract_text_from_part(part: email.message.EmailMessage) -> str: """ Return the best textual representation of a single part. * text/plain → decode & return * text/html → decode → optional HTML→text conversion * other → empty string (handled elsewhere) """ ctype = part.get_content_type() if ctype == "text/plain": return _decode_payload(part) if ctype == "text/html": html = _decode_payload(part) return _html_to_text(html) # Not a text part we can render return "" def _walk_message(msg: email.message.EmailMessage) -> dict: """ Walk the message tree, returning: { "headers": dict of selected header fields, "body": plain‑text body (first suitable part found), "attachments": [ {"filename": str, "content_type": str, "size": int}, … ] } """ # --- collect a few nice‑to‑have headers (feel free to extend) --- header_fields = ["Subject", "From", "To", "Cc", "Bcc", "Date", "Message-ID"] headers = {h: msg[h] for h in header_fields if h in msg} # --- find textual body ------------------------------------------------- # Prefer a plain‑text part, otherwise fall back to HTML → text. body_text = None # Attachments are collected separately attachments = [] # Queue for BFS (handles nested multiparts nicely) queue = [msg] while queue: part = queue.pop(0) if part.is_multipart(): # Enqueue its sub‑parts for later processing queue.extend(part.iter_parts()) continue ctype = part.get_content_type() disposition = part.get_content_disposition() # None, "inline", "attachment" if disposition == "attachment": # Record metadata (we don't write the file, but you can) filename = part.get_filename() size = len(part.get_payload(decode=True) or b"") attachments.append({ "filename": filename, "content_type": ctype, "size": size, }) continue # If we reach here the part is a *single* (non‑multipart) body part # Try to extract text: text = _extract_text_from_part(part) if text: # If we haven't yet captured any body, take this one. # If we already have a body and this part is plain‑text while the existing # one came from HTML, replace it (plain‑text is usually cleaner). if body_text is None: body_text = text elif "text/html" in ctype and "text/plain" not in ctype: # keep what we already have (prefer plain over html) pass else: # For messages that contain multiple plain parts (e.g. signatures), # concatenate them with a separator. body_text = body_text.rstrip() + "\n\n---\n\n" + text # If there was no explicit text part, but there were HTML parts that we ignored # because of missing bs4, try a final HTML‑to‑text conversion on the raw payload. if body_text is None: # As a last resort, pull the raw payload of the top‑level message try: raw = msg.get_payload(decode=True) or b"" body_text = raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace") except Exception: body_text = "" return { "headers": headers, "body": body_text or "", "attachments": attachments, } # ---------------------------------------------------------------------- # Public helper # ---------------------------------------------------------------------- def extract_eml_to_text(eml_path: str | Path) -> str: """ Read *eml_path* and return a ready‑to‑print plain‑text representation.     db.init_app(app)
```python
    migrate.init_app(app, db)
    login_manager.init_app(app)
    jwt.init_app(app)
    cors.init_app(app, resources={r"/api/*": {"origins": "*"}})

    # Register blueprints
    app.register_blueprint(api_bp, url_prefix="/api")

    # Simple health endpoint
    @app.route("/health")
    def health():
        return jsonify({"status":"ok"}), 200

    return app

# Needed for Celery to discover the Flask app context
def make_celery(app=None):
    app = app or create_app()
    celery.conf.update(app.config)
    TaskBase = celery.Task

    class ContextTask(TaskBase):
        abstract = True
        def __call__(self, *args, **kwargs):
            with app.app_context():
                return TaskBase.__call__(self, *args, **kwargs)

    celery.Task = ContextTask
    return celery
```

```python
        password_hash=generate_password_hash(data["password"])
    )
```

## 5️⃣ Social‑Media Integration Scaffolding  

All platforms use **OAuth 2.0** (or OAuth 1.0a for old Twitter).  
Below are tiny wrappers that you can call from routes or Celery tasks.

> **Tip:** Store the **client_id / client_secret** in environment variables (`.env`).  

### Common OAuth helper (`backend/utils/oauth.py`)

```python
import requests
from urllib.parse import urlencode

def get_authorization_url(base_url, client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state=None, extra_params=None):
    """
    Returns the URL the user must be redirected to for OAuth consent.
    """
    params = {
        "client_id": client_id,
        "redirect_uri": redirect_uri,
        "response_type": "code",
        "scope": " ".join(scope),
    }
    if state:
        params["state"] = state
    if extra_params:
        params.update(extra_params)
    return f"{base_url}?{urlencode(params)}"

def exchange_code_for_token(token_url, client_id, client_secret, code, redirect_uri):
    """
    Generic POST request to swap a code for an access token.
    """
    resp = requests.post(token_url, data={
        "grant_type": "authorization_code",
        "code": code,
        "redirect_uri": redirect_uri,
        "client_id": client_id,
        "client_secret": client_secret,
    })
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()   # contains access_token, expires_in, refresh_token, etc.
```

```python
def get_auth_url(state: str = None):
    scope = ["pages_manage_posts", "pages_read_engagement", "pages_manage_engagement",
             "pages_show_list", "instagram_basic", "ads_read"]
    return get_authorization_url(AUTH_URL, CLIENT_ID, REDIRECT_URI, scope, state)

def get_token(code: str):
    return exchange_code_for_token(TOKEN_URL, CLIENT_ID,
                                   CLIENT_SECRET, code, REDIRECT_URI)

def post_to_page(page_id: str, message: str, link: str = None, media_url: str = None,
                 access_token: str = None):
    """
    Publishes a post on a Facebook Page.
    """
    endpoint = f"{GRAPH_API}/{page_id}/feed"
    payload = {"message": message, "access_token": access_token}
    if link:
        payload["link"] = link
    if media_url:
        # For photos we need a separate call; this is a simplified version.
        payload["picture"] = media_url
    resp = requests.post(endpoint, data=payload)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()   # contains "id"
```

```python
        "grant_type": "authorization_code",
        "code": code,
        "redirect_uri": REDIRECT_URI,
        "client_id": CLIENT_ID,
        "client_secret": CLIENT_SECRET,
    })
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()

def post_ugc(urn_author, text, access_token, media_urn=None):
    """
    Posts a User‑Generated Content (UGC) post.
    `urn_author` = "urn:li:person:xxxx"
    """
    endpoint = "https://api.linkedin.com/v2/ugcPosts"
    payload = {
        "author": urn_author,
        "lifecycleState": "PUBLISHED",
        "specificContent": {
            "com.linkedin.ugc.ShareContent": {
                "shareCommentary": {"text": text},
                "shareMediaCategory": "NONE"
            }
        },
        "visibility": {"com.linkedin.ugc.MemberNetworkVisibility": "PUBLIC"}
    }
    if media_urn:
        payload["specificContent"]["com.linkedin.ugc.ShareContent"]["shareMediaCategory"] = "IMAGE"
        payload["specificContent"]["com.linkedin.ugc.ShareContent"]["media"] = [
            {"status": "READY", "description": {"text": ""}, "media": media_urn, "title": {"text": ""}}
        ]
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}",
               "X-Restli-Protocol-Version":"2.0.0",
               "Content-Type": "application/json"}
    resp = requests.post(endpoint, headers=headers, json=payload)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()
```
